title: Methods
bridge: Java's functions are **methods**, and they declare the type of every parameter and of what they return: `static double area(double w, double h) { return w * h; }`. `void` means it returns nothing. Two methods can share a name if their parameters differ (**overloading**).

exercises.title: Temperatures
exercises.prompt: Write cToF(double c) and fToC(double f) (F = C × 9/5 + 32), each rounded to 1 decimal: Math.round(x * 10) / 10.0.

exercises.title: Overloading
exercises.prompt: Write two methods called total: total(int qty, double unitPrice) returns qty × price, and total(int qty, double unitPrice, double discountPercent) applies the discount. Round both to 2 decimals.
hints: Two methods with the same name and different parameters.
The 2-argument one can call the 3-argument one with discount 0.

exercises.title: One job each
exercises.prompt: Write clean(String name) (trim + capitalise first letter, rest lower), fmtKg(double kg) giving "40.0 kg", and line(String name, double kg) that uses both: "Amina: 40.0 kg".

quiz.q: Two methods named area with different parameters is…
A method changes its int parameter. Does the caller's variable change?
choices: No: Java passes a copy of simple values

cards.q: Parts of a Java method header?
Format a double to 1 decimal as text?

explain: Explain methods to someone who has never programmed, in your own words, with an example you make up.
